```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(tidyverse)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
```

# Data

Long-form feature listing data (one row per participant, cue, and feature word). All idiosyncratic responses are kept.

```{r load-data}
fl <- read_csv("../data/08_words.csv")
glimpse(fl)
```

```{r data-summary}
fl %>%
  summarise(
    participants = n_distinct(subject_id),
    cues = n_distinct(cue),
    features = n_distinct(word),
    rows = n()
  )
```

# Predictors

## Concreteness norms

TODO: add a concreteness norm file (for example Brysbaert et al., 2014) to `data/` and join it for both cues and features.

```{r concreteness, eval=FALSE}
conc <- read_csv("../data/concreteness_norms.csv") # word, concreteness

fl <- fl %>%
  left_join(conc %>% rename(cue = word, cue_concrete = concreteness), by = "cue") %>%
  left_join(conc %>% rename(word = word, feature_concrete = concreteness), by = "word")
```

# Cue concreteness vs. feature concreteness

Using targets (features) as Y and cues as X, we expect a strong correlation but also a higher intercept (Dunning-Kruger-like pattern?).

```{r correlation, eval=FALSE}
fl %>%
  distinct(cue, word, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  summarise(r = cor(cue_concrete, feature_concrete, use = "complete.obs"))

ggplot(fl, aes(cue_concrete, feature_concrete)) +
  geom_point(alpha = .05) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") +
  theme_minimal()
```

# Mixed model

```{r model, eval=FALSE}
m1 <- lmer(
  feature_concrete ~ cue_concrete + sem_distance + feature_frequency:sem_distance +
    (1 | subject_id) + (1 | cue),
  data = fl
)
summary(m1)
```

The planned structure was `(participant | cue)`; adjust the random effects if the model fails to converge.
